clue.text: Plant part on 1 dn. Jeremy

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: Jeremy plus the answer to 1 Down names Beatrix Potter's angling character Mr Jeremy, who is a frog
a part is a bit, a piece of something

explanation.surface: Instructions to find a plant growing on some part of a character called Jeremy.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference makes Jeremy Fisher, the frog in Beatrix Potter's children's stories, so the 'Jeremy' is a frog; 'on' puts BIT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small floating water weed, a pond species named for the amphibians that share its habitat.

clue.text: Evangelist who may be after a King

definitions.meaning: Christ called his disciples to be ... of men, so a preacher seeking converts

definitions.text: who may be after a King
definitions.meaning: placed after King it makes the name of the brightly coloured river bird

explanation.definitionFit: A preacher wins souls as a fisher of men; and put after 'king' the word names the bird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Starts shelling peas, say — no use otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise asks for the letters of the pair of Ps and no use in another order
say signals that the sound of the word, not its spelling, gives the letters

parts.note: the word peas spoken sounds like the letter P twice over

explanation.surface: Someone begins shelling peas, though there's no use in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns 'peas' into PP; 'otherwise' rearranges PP with NOUSE. Shelling peas tempts a kitchen picture, but the shelling is artillery fire.
explanation.definitionFit: When guns open up they begin firing; to commence bombardment is to begin shelling.

clue.text: Programme using American female players

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A show featuring American actresses.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD is dated US slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television transmission is a programme sent out to listeners or viewers.

clue.text: Very tough examination for advanced academic award?

definitions.meaning: playfully, a degree beyond a second one in level

explanation.definitionFit: Severe questioning by police is the idiom; and the question mark admits a whimsical university qualification one step beyond bachelor's and master's.

clue.text: Man promoted by Earl of Warwick?

definitions.text: Man promoted by Earl of Warwick?

parts.words: Man promoted by Earl of Warwick?
parts.note: the Earl of Warwick was the Kingmaker; a board-game piece that reaches the far row is crowned, made a king

explanation.surface: A courtier raised in rank by the medieval Earl of Warwick.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, was nicknamed the Kingmaker. A 'man' is also a playing piece, and in this board game a man reaching the last row is crowned king, so a kingmaker promotes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece in the board game (checkers in America) that becomes a king when it reaches the far side is promoted.

clue.text: One put, for a bet, in Dante's Inferno

indicators.note: the numeral is put in place of the bet, so one takes over the bet's position

parts.note: the poet's name with its possessive S
an ante is a stake put into a poker pot
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone places a wager in Dante's famous poem about hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put, for' replaces ANTE in DANTES with I. 'Dante's Inferno' looks like the title, but only 'Inferno' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical myth and in Dante's poem this is the name of the underworld city, a lower hell.

clue.text: Taking part of writer, leaves producer

parts.note: acting as someone is taking their part
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author acts the role of a writer and quits a film producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is a noun: the definition is a producer of leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This poplar with trembling foliage is a tree, and trees grow leaves.

clue.text: To obtain satisfaction, double the odds?

definitions.meaning: to take revenge, settle the score
multiplying any odd number by two makes it divisible by two

explanation.definitionFit: Settling a score is having revenge; and doubling an odd number always yields a number divisible by two.

clue.text: Vehicles for publicity

explanation.definitionFit: Towed wheeled units are vehicles; and short previews of coming films are advertising.

clue.text: History master takes us both ways round school before one

indicators.note: the two copies of the word us sit around the school and the one
the word us appears read backwards and also forwards, so it is used in both directions

parts.note: taken as written, then turned
taken as written

indicators.note: the school comes ahead of the one

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A history teacher takes the class both ways around the school grounds before one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' makes 'us' serve twice, once backwards and once forwards; 'round' wraps that pair about the school-plus-one, which 'before' orders. The Roman writer of The Twelve Caesars is the master.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman biographer who wrote The Twelve Caesars was a great ancient historian, a master of history.

clue.text: City there for half-time

parts.note: alludes to the famous line describing a rose-red city half as old as time

explanation.surface: A city where one stays for the half-time interval.
explanation.walkthrough: John Burgon's poem calls this Jordanian site 'a rose-red city half as old as time', so it has been there for half of time; 'half-time' pretends to be a football break.
explanation.definitionFit: This rock-cut ancient city in Jordan was famously described in verse as being half as old as time itself.

clue.text: Sea-storm between point and Land's End abated

indicators.note: the shuffled sea goes between the point and the end of Land

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: the end of the word Land is its last letter
storm signals the letters of sea being thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm at sea between a headland and Land's End died down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' is the anagram signal on 'Sea', and 'between' places the result inside the point and the end letter; Land's End is Cornwall's westernmost tip, read here as the last letter of 'Land'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean lessened or died down, as a storm or pain does when its force weakens.

clue.text: Book for those without a lot of sense, so to speak

definitions.text: Book for those without a lot of sense, so to speak

parts.words: Book for those without a lot of sense, so to speak
parts.note: sense said aloud is cents: a cheap book costing a ten-cent coin suits those with little money

explanation.surface: A book suited to readers who are rather lacking in good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sense, so to speak' sounds like cents; a ten-cent coin bought the cheap American popular fiction of the nineteenth century, so it suited those without many cents.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational paperback once sold for ten cents, so a book for readers without much money, and arguably without much taste.

clue.text: Overcome stonewaller who's passed 4

definitions.note: one who has passed the answer to 4 Down, the Freemasons' highest craft rank

parts.note: to overcome is to master
a mason builds walls from stone

explanation.surface: A defensive batsman who has passed four is finally beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: A stonewaller is a cricket batsman who blocks every ball, but here a builder of stone walls. Freemasonry's top craft grade is called the third degree.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freemasonry the third and highest craft rank is conferred on a member who has passed through the earlier grades.

clue.text: By no means exclusive place for West End address

definitions.text: By no means exclusive place for West End address

parts.words: By no means exclusive place for West End address
parts.note: a London spot where anyone at all may stand up and deliver a speech, an address in the West End

explanation.surface: A far from exclusive spot to have a postal address in London's fashionable West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' reads as a postal address in the smart West End, London's theatre and shopping district, but it means a speech; the spot in Hyde Park is open to anyone wanting to orate.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-east corner of Hyde Park is a traditional open-air venue where any member of the public may make a speech.

clue.text: Dismissed vulgar women from border area

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
skirt is vulgar slang for women

explanation.surface: Coarse women thrown out of a frontier zone.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIRT is crude slang for women.
explanation.definitionFit: The fringes of a town are the area at its edge or border.

clue.text: Defeats in Davis Cup persistently

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie inside the run of words Davis Cup persistently

explanation.surface: Repeated losses in the Davis Cup tennis competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters inside 'DaviS CUP PERSistently'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck or thwart a plan is to sink it, as a ship is deliberately sunk; so it beats or foils.

clue.text: Criminals wrongly set free in court

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of set free in court are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers mistakenly released at a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges all fourteen letters of SET FREE IN COURT; the surface tempts a container with the anagram inside COURT, but every word is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgers of money or goods are lawbreakers, so they fit the general word for offenders.

clue.text: Jack's absence from meeting-place at first affected enthusiasm

indicators.note: absence from says the jack is missing from the word for meeting-place
at first says the letter goes missing from the very front

parts.note: a junction is where roads or lines meet
J is the card abbreviation for a jack

explanation.surface: A missing friend called Jack first dampened everyone's eagerness at the rendezvous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absence from' and 'at first' remove the J from the front of JUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: This word can mean an oily, insincere earnestness, a show of fervour that is put on.

clue.text: Continuing to play without a break

definitions.meaning: still being staged, as a long-lasting show
consecutive, as in three days in a row

explanation.definitionFit: A show still being staged is said to be in its run; and days in a row follow each other without interruption.

clue.text: Woody part of New York

definitions.meaning: leafy, shaded like an arbour of trees
a street and district of lower Manhattan

explanation.definitionFit: Like a leafy arbour means tree-shaded; and the street in lower Manhattan is a well-known district.

clue.text: My dear chap, it's absurd to remove a large beast

indicators.note: absurd signals that the letters of my dear chap are jumbled, here after one letter is taken out

parts.note: the full pool of letters
the letter taken away from the pool, signalled by remove

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend it would be ridiculous to try shifting a huge animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' with 'to remove a' is a composite anagram: take the A out of MY DEAR CHAP and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants, rhinos and hippos are thick-skinned mammals, all of them very big animals.

clue.text: Brute produces upset in dancing circles

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the dance's letters upside down, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: the hay is an old English country dance
two circles look like two letter Os

explanation.surface: A thug causes upheaval at dance clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The hay (or hey) is an old country dance; 'upset' turns it to YAH. The brutes are the human beasts in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swift's Gulliver's Travels these are degraded human beasts, so the word means a coarse lout.

clue.text: Type of combat to finish in conclusive result

indicators.note: the word for finishing goes inside the knockout

parts.note: a knockout, KO, is the decisive result of a boxing bout
to finish is to end

explanation.surface: A form of fighting meant to end in a decisive victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts END inside KO, the knockout abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords is a form of combat sport.

clue.text: Miss ebb at Southend?

definitions.meaning: an unmarried woman with a girl's name, here a forename
an ebb tide as said with the dropped consonants of an Essex or Estuary accent

explanation.walkthrough: Southend is a seaside town in Essex; the setter's joke is that 'ebb tide', in the local Estuary English accent, comes out as the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Miss can be addressed by forename, here a once-common girl's name; and the falling tide at Southend, spoken in the local accent, sounds just like it.

clue.text: Worshipping maids are doubly so

parts.note: people at church are attending worship, and maids are domestic employees: two senses of one phrase

explanation.surface: Housemaids who are at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Maids are employed as servants, and when they are at church they are also attending worship, so the phrase applies to them twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a church service means worshipping, and domestic servants such as maids were said to be employed in someone's household.

clue.text: Accommodation within Swiss banks initially

definitions.meaning: a river that rises in Switzerland, so its first stretch runs between Swiss banks

explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry offers lodging; and the river rising in the Engadine flows first through Switzerland before Austria and Germany.

clue.text: Star's disappearance — paper has a sort of clue

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
a down is one sort of crossword clue, the other being across

explanation.surface: A newspaper's crossword clue about a celebrity vanishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Star' is the Sun itself, not a celebrity; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is when our nearest star sinks below the horizon and disappears from view.

clue.text: Lack of influence about, for instance, flowers

indicators.note: the phrase for no influence goes round the letters for instance

parts.note: having no say is lacking influence
eg, for example

explanation.surface: Someone without influence on matters concerning flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NO SAY around EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy or bunch of blooms, often scented, is a gathering of cut blossoms.
